questions.question: A 4 cm long chord subtends a central angle of 60°. The radial segment of this circle is:
questions.explanation: In triangle OAB, OA = OB = r and central angle is 60°. The remaining angles are (180° - 60°)/2 = 60°, so OAB is equilateral. Thus r = chord = 4 cm.

questions.question: The length of a chord and the radial segment of a circle are congruent. The central angle made by the chord will be:
questions.explanation: When chord = radius, all three sides of the triangle formed by the centre and chord endpoints are equal (equilateral), so central angle = 60°.

questions.question: Out of two congruent arcs of a circle, if one arc subtends a central angle of 30°, the other arc will subtend a central angle of:
questions.explanation: Theorem 1 of Unit 11: Congruent arcs subtend equal central angles in the same circle (or congruent circles).

questions.question: An arc subtends a central angle of 40°. Then the corresponding chord will subtend a central angle of:
questions.explanation: The chord connects the same endpoints as the arc; its central angle is identically 40°.

questions.question: If two arcs of a circle are congruent, then their corresponding chords are:
questions.explanation: Theorem: If two arcs of a circle are congruent, their corresponding chords are equal in length.

questions.question: If two chords of a circle are equal in length, their corresponding minor arcs are:
questions.explanation: Converse theorem: Equal chords cut off congruent minor (and major) arcs.

questions.question: An arc of a circle whose measure is less than that of a semicircle is called a/an:
questions.explanation: An arc subtending less than 180° at the centre is defined as a minor arc.

questions.question: An arc of a circle whose measure is greater than that of a semicircle is called a/an:
questions.explanation: An arc subtending more than 180° at the centre is a major arc.

questions.question: An arc having measure equal to half of the circle's circumference is called a:
questions.explanation: Half of the circumference subtending 180° at the centre is a semicircle.

questions.question: If an arc subtends a central angle of 90°, the ratio of the chord length to radius r is:
questions.explanation: In right triangle with legs r, r, hypotenuse chord = √(r² + r²) = r√2. Ratio chord/r = √2.

questions.question: Equal chords of a circle subtend central angles that are:
questions.explanation: Triangles formed by radii and equal chords are congruent by SSS, so their central angles are equal.

questions.question: The sum of the central angles of all non-overlapping adjacent sectors forming a complete circle is:
questions.explanation: The total angle around the central point of a circle is 360°.

questions.question: If arc AB has length equal to the circumference of the circle divided by 6, its central angle is:
questions.explanation: Central angle = 360° / 6 = 60°.

questions.question: If chord AB = chord CD in a circle, then:
questions.explanation: Equal chords intercept arcs of equal degree measure.

questions.question: In a circle with radius 5 cm, the perimeter of a semicircle (including diameter) is:
questions.explanation: Perimeter = arc + diameter = πr + 2r = 5π + 10 cm.

questions.question: Two arcs of the same circle are congruent if they have:

options.A: The same degree measure (or equal lengths)

questions.explanation: In a given circle, arcs are congruent if and only if their central angle measures (and lengths) are equal.

questions.question: A chord subtending a central angle of 180° is a:
questions.explanation: A central angle of 180° forms a straight line through the centre, which is the diameter.

questions.question: If the minor arc AB is 100°, then the corresponding major arc AB is:
questions.explanation: Major arc = 360° - minor arc = 360° - 100° = 260°.

questions.question: Congruent circles have equal:
questions.explanation: Circles are congruent if and only if their radii (or diameters) are equal.

questions.question: If chord AB = 10 cm and chord CD = 10 cm in the same circle, the arcs AB and CD are:
questions.explanation: Chords of equal length in a circle intercept congruent arcs.
